en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Training Rule on Being Veiled.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were teaching the Dhamma to one who had his head covered... [etc. ...
"The training is to be observed: 'I shall not teach the Dhamma to one with a covered head who is not ill.
One with a covered head means:
"One whose head is covered" means one who has wrapped [the head] with a cloth.
The Dhamma must not be taught to one who is not ill and has his head covered.
Whoever, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma to one who is not ill and has his head covered, commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense if it was unintentional,
or if there was a lack of mindfulness.
If he instructs after having had the head uncovered for one who is unaware or for one who is ill.
The seventh training rule is concluded.
